name: Evaluation Datasets
blurb: Benchmarks and test sets, and what each actually measures.

items.note: Grade-school math word problems; the standard arithmetic-reasoning test
Science exam questions in easy and challenge splits
57-subject knowledge exam; the most-cited general capability benchmark
The successor suite to GLUE for language understanding
Commonsense sentence completion designed to be adversarial to models
164 hand-written programming problems; the original code-generation benchmark
The harder ten-choice successor as frontier models saturated MMLU
Graduate-level science questions that resist search; gated to keep answers out of training data

reading.body:
GSM8K leads all evaluation datasets with 1.14 million downloads, more than double the next closest, which signals that arithmetic reasoning is the most actively tested capability in the field right now.

The download counts reveal a rough hierarchy of what practitioners are measuring. Math and factual knowledge benchmarks cluster at the top. Code generation and instruction-following sit in the middle tier. The presence of MMLU-Pro, a harder successor created specifically because frontier models saturated the original MMLU, shows the field cycling through benchmarks as models exhaust them. That cycling matters for compute planning: a benchmark that is saturated stops producing signal, which forces new evaluation work and, eventually, new training runs designed to close gaps on harder tests.

GPQA is the only gated dataset in this set, and its gatekeeping is intentional. The note records that access is restricted to keep answers out of training data, which is a different kind of infrastructure problem from power or buildings, but a real one. A benchmark that leaks into pretraining corpora no longer measures what it claims to measure. The data here covers download volume and licensing terms but does not say how often these benchmarks appear in training sets, how current their difficulty ceilings are relative to the latest models, or how representative their question distributions are of real-world AI use.
